newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS-Telefonica sale seen as big success.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Telefonica sale seen as big success.

text.p: Spain's sale of its final stake in telecoms operator Telefonica was seen on Tuesday as an unqualified success and a big step toward building a new investment culture in the country.
"The success of the flotation attracted new funds to the bourse and paved the way for the next set of privatisations," one brokerage dealer said.
More than 1.2 million small investors took part in the flotation -- the biggest in Spain and one of the biggest in Europe -- many of them buying stocks for the first time.
Telefonica de Espana had made a particular effort to attract mom and pop investors in its pre-sale publicity campaign, echoing the populist appeal of its first offer in the 1960s.

The original shares were affectionately called "matildes" after a radio and television spot that had a man on a street shouting up to his wife, "Matilde, let's go, the shares in Telefonica are ready".
They became one of the most rock solid in the bourse in the 1970s and 80s.

The Spanish public's demand for Telefonica shares this time around was so overwhelming -- nine times the offer -- the state holding company SEPPa was just barely able to stick to a promised 100 share minimum for every subscriber.
SEPPa boosted the number of shares going to the retail tranche to 114 million or 67 percent of the total offer due to the "oversubscription of this magnitude".

But the market had no trouble absorbing the 171 million new shares early on Tuesday and Telefonica was quoting unchanged at the institutional tranche price of 3,360 pesetas with some three million shares traded in just 90 minutes.

"It's been a great success along general lines," one analyst said. "The extremely elevated demand forced the amplification of the retail tranche to 67 percent and in a short time the share should restart its upward march."

Spanish analysts said the success of Telefonica's sale showed that the bourse was becoming more attractive for investors at a time when foreign stock exchanges are strong and bond yields have been falling.
Investment funds dealing on the stock market have seen a huge surge in interest in the past few weeks with assets growing from 470 billion pesetas to 1.4 trillion in January.
"With the interest rates the way they are, it's logical that people would direct their savings into the stock market," another dealer said.

Analysts said Telefonica's easy absorption was a sign that the bourse was well placed to take on the state's other planned privatisations: energy firm Repsol, electricity utility Endesa and bank Argentaria.

Participants in Telefonica's last share offer in October 1995 doubled their investment if they did not get nervous and pull out in the first week of the placement when the share price plummeted 11 percent.
Telefonica got back on track then, outperforming the general bourse index last year with an 80 percent gain against the index rise of 40 percent, and is expected to rise again.
"The privatisation was a great success and within two or three months, the share should return to gains," a trader said.
